t: A land dispute between the Southern Pacific Railroad and settlers in Hanford, California, turned deadly when a gun battle broke out, leaving seven dead.
"O Canada", the present-day national anthem of Canada, was first performed in Quebec City during a Saint-Jean-Baptiste Day banquet.
Police captured Australian bank robber and cultural icon Ned Kelly after a gun battle in Glenrowan, Victoria.
James A. Garfield was elected as president of the United States; the election is the closest to date by popular vote margin.
The current melody of Kimigayo, the national anthem of Japan, was adopted.
In spite of sympathizers holding rallies for his reprieve, Australian bushranger and outlaw Ned Kelly was hanged in Melbourne.
At an assembly of 10,000 Boers, Paul Kruger announced the fulfilment of the decision to restore the government and volksraad of the South African Republic.
